# Aristotle: Subject-Predicate-Object Triples

## Life & Identity
- Aristotle, was born in, 384 BCE
- Aristotle, died in, 322 BCE
- Aristotle, was born in, Stagira
- Aristotle, was a, philosopher
- Aristotle, was a, polymath
- Aristotle, had nationality, Ancient Macedonian/Greek

## Education & Teachers
- Aristotle, studied under, Plato
- Aristotle, attended, Plato's Academy
- Aristotle, spent years in, Athens

## Professional Life
- Aristotle, founded, the Lyceum
- Aristotle, taught at, the Lyceum
- Aristotle, tutored, Alexander the Great
- Aristotle, was employed by, Philip II of Macedon
- Aristotle, worked in, Athens

## Major Works
- Aristotle, wrote, Metaphysics
- Aristotle, wrote, Nicomachean Ethics
- Aristotle, wrote, Politics
- Aristotle, wrote, Rhetoric
- Aristotle, wrote, Poetics
- Aristotle, wrote, Physics
- Aristotle, wrote, Categories
- Aristotle, wrote, Prior Analytics
- Aristotle, wrote, Posterior Analytics

## Philosophical Contributions
- Aristotle, developed, logic system (syllogism)
- Aristotle, developed, theory of causation
- Aristotle, developed, virtue ethics
- Aristotle, developed, theory of forms critique
- Aristotle, emphasized, empirical observation
- Aristotle, advocated for, systematic classification

## Key Concepts
- Aristotle, believed in, teleology (purpose in nature)
- Aristotle, defined, eudaimonia as, happiness/flourishing
- Aristotle, promoted, the golden mean
- Aristotle, categorized, substances and properties
- Aristotle, described, unmoved mover (God)

## Influences & Legacy
- Aristotle, was influenced by, Plato
- Aristotle, influenced, medieval Islamic philosophy
- Aristotle, influenced, medieval European thought
- Aristotle, influenced, Thomas Aquinas
- Aristotle, influenced, modern science
- Aristotle, established, foundational logic

## Disagreements
- Aristotle, disagreed with, Plato on forms
- Aristotle, rejected, Plato's theory of forms
